subject: Data retention exception request — FinSecure PII flows
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsecure.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finsecure.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + FinSecure requirements

Camila — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap for my team: FinSecure will be evaluating Redwood for transaction-monitoring features that will process customer-provided PII. A couple of hard constraints from legal/security: 1) no retention of raw PII logs beyond session (we call this 0-retention); 2) audit logs must be pseudonymized and retained for 30 days only; 3) data residency: EU for EU customers, US for US customers.

Can Redwood support a contractual exception for 0-retention of PII-derived logs, and a shortened access/log retention window? If so, what is the operational approach and changes to the DPA?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, FinSecure
alex.j@finsecure.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsecure.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@finsecure.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request — FinSecure PII flows

Alex — really appreciate the clear recap and the specific asks. Next steps from our side: I wanted to loop in Neha (Legal) and Rafael (Solutions) to confirm feasibility and propose the operational guardrails.

High-level answers up front: we have patterns for reduced retention for sensitive fields, and we support region-specific processing. A few follow-ups we need to confirm with your team to scope the exception:

- Which exact fields do you categorize as PII for this flow? (e.g., full name, SSN, account numbers, full address)
- Are you okay with on-the-fly pseudonymization before any logs are written, or do you require zero-write of those raw elements?
- Do you have any downstream analytics that will require access to de-identified aggregates beyond 30 days?

I attached a simple retention_matrix.xlsx that maps typical log types -> default retention -> suggested FinSecure exception. If we can get the field list and confirmation on aggregates, Rafael and Neha will draft the exception language for the DPA and a runtime plan.

Proposed timeline: 2 business days to confirm field list, 3 business days for an internal feasibility + DPA mark-up, then a joint call to finalize.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
[Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data retention exception request — FinSecure PII flows

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read: we can include a limited retention exception in the DPA but need to be explicit about the scope and controls. Key items we will require operationally for the exception:

- Exact dataset / field list (as Camila requested).
- A signed addendum to the DPA specifying 0-retention fields and retention windows for pseudonymized logs.
- Proof that pseudonymization is irreversible (or uses salted hashing with customer-controlled salt) and that no raw PII persists in any logs/backups/snapshots.
- Audit evidence for any deletion/retention workflows (automated deletion job logs, retention policy configs).

Rafael — can you confirm whether we can configure the runtime to avoid writing raw fields into token logs and whether we can implement an automated zero-retention pipeline for specific fields? If not fully possible, what mitigations (e.g., immediate masking, customer-managed encryption keys) are feasible?

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data retention exception request — FinSecure PII flows

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:05 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rafael — can you confirm whether we can configure the runtime to avoid writing raw fields into token logs and whether we can implement an automated zero-retention pipeline for specific fields? If not fully possible, what mitigations (e.g., immediate masking, customer-managed encryption keys) are feasible?

Thanks — quick technical summary and proposed customer response:

1) Zero-write for raw PII: we can implement a pre-ingest transform on the customer route that strips or pseudonymizes configured fields before they hit any persistent logs. That transform runs in the edge proxy (no persistence) and forwards only tokenized/pseudonymized payloads to the inference pool. Implementation estimate: ~5 business days for route-specific config + test.

2) Audit logs / operational logs: by default we capture limited operational logs. For FinSecure we can: a) pseudonymize identifiers in logs, b) configure retention to 30 days, and c) run an automated deletion job that purges any residual indexes or backups containing those fields. We will provide job output as proof-of-deletion.

3) DPA addendum: Rafael recommends language that states "Redwood will not persist raw PII for configured fields; pseudonymization is performed prior to any persistent logging. Audit evidence of deletion will be provided on request." Neha — if legal is comfortable, we can put a draft into the DPA and offer DocuSign link when ready.

Action items I propose we confirm with FinSecure on the joint call:
- Provide exact list of PII fields to be zero-written.
- Confirm acceptable pseudonymization approach (hashing with customer salt vs one-way tokenization).
- Agree on post-deployment verification steps and frequency (e.g., one-time validation + quarterly attestations).

Alex / Morgan — happy to hop on a 30-min technical sync tomorrow to walk through the flow and show the retention_matrix. If that works I can send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
